title: Specified inverse-image comparison is the completion unit
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below have $\ell$ invertible and use small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For each scheme $W$, set $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ of $B_{W,n}$-modules with quotient-linear transitions, and its unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $\mathcal R_W$ for simultaneous derived reduction, $U_W$ for exact restriction to $\widehat R_W$-module towers and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim U_W$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $G=g^{-1}$ on completed module complexes, transporting scalars through $g^{-1}\widehat R_Y\cong\widehat R_X$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Write $P_g=Lg^*$ for completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and let $\kappa^g_N:GN\to P_gN$ be the SPECIFIED map of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b). For any ambient complex $N\in D(\widehat R_Y)$ define $\widehat N=\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YN$ and let $u_N:N\to\widehat N$ be the actual unit of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_{g,N}:P_gN\xrightarrow{\sim}G\widehat N$$
such that
$$\theta_{g,N}\circ\kappa^g_N=G(u_N).$$
Here $\theta$ is the map of entire strict quotient cones induced by multiplication $g^*Q_n\to GQ_n$, $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, and the product/cone comparison for the exact site equivalence, for one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to N$. The displayed equation specifies the zero shifted-coordinate cone map, not only its projections. It is independent of $Q$ under the canonical resolution comparisons and natural for derived morphisms. In particular, if $N$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], then this specified $\kappa^g_N$ is invertible, with inverse $G(u_N)^{-1}\theta_{g,N}$. No invertibility is asserted for incomplete ambient objects, and no equality with an unspecified choice of the isomorphism $\lambda_N$ is assumed.

source.place: Clause (2), pullback commutes with reductions, and clause (3), second paragraph: agent-formulated identification of the specified inverse-image comparison with the completion unit. Compare Stacks derived.tex Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit) and the explicit cone map of def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison (b).

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $N$ and a flat-term K-flat quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Set $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}B_{Y,n}$, $r_n(x)=x\otimes1$, and $\tau_n=1\otimes(B_{Y,n+1}\to B_{Y,n})$. The simultaneous reduction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] is represented by the strict semilinear complex $TQ=(Q_n,\tau_n)$, not merely by its evaluations. Put $D=U_Y(TQ)$ and $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g^*Q_n$, with the strict transitions of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Products in both completed module categories are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. For any of these strict towers $Z$ write $H(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Z)[-1]$. In coordinates $H(Z)^i=(\prod_n Z_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod_n Z_n^i)$, its differential is $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_Z)a,da)$. By [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], $H(D)$ realizes $\widehat N$ and $H(C)$ realizes $P_gN$, with the normalized total-limit identifications. Since $\tau_nr_{n+1}=r_n$, the formula $v_Q(z)=(0,(r_nz)_n)$ is a chain map $Q\to H(D)$.

source.place: Clauses (2)-(3): simultaneous quotient model; Stacks Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 08TC (definition-derived-limit), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok).

proof.text: Identify the actual unit, rather than selecting a lift of its projections. In the sequence ringed site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], let $T$ denote simultaneous underived extension and $V=\lim U$. Their ordinary adjunction sends $f=(f_n):TQ\to M$ to $z\mapsto(f_n(z\otimes1))_n\in VM$; its inverse sends $h:Q\to VM$ to $z\otimes a\mapsto a h_n(z)$. These formulas are balanced, respect transitions and are inverse. Choose $a:TQ\to I$ K-injective with injective terms in the semilinear category and $j:UI\to J$ K-injective with injective terms in the constant-ring tower category; these are ringed-site resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The derived-adjunction fraction formula [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], applied to the canonical adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], transposes the identity of $\mathcal R_YN$, represented by $a$ on this left-derived model, to $Q\to VI$, $z\mapsto(a_nr_nz)_n$, followed by $VI\to\lim J$. This last map is the canonical right-derived composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]: factor the sequence projection as restriction of rings (direct image $U$) followed by the constant-ring sequence projection (direct image $\lim$). Its normalization is exactly $\lim j$, so the composite represents $u_N$ after $[q]^{-1}$. All sites are small in the fixed module universe. No preservation of K-injectives by $U$ is assumed.

source.place: Clause (3): agent refinement identifying the canonical derived adjunction unit; Bhatt-Scholze Definition 3.5.2 and Lemma 3.5.7(1); normalized derived-adjunction fraction calculation.

proof.text: Let $b= j\circ U(a):D\to J$. This is a quasi-isomorphism of entire strict towers. On both cone coordinates $H(b)$ is the product of the $b_n$. Therefore $H(b)v_Q(z)=(0,(j_na_nr_nz)_n)$. The composite $Q\to VI\xrightarrow{\lim j}\lim J\to H(J)$ of step 2 has exactly this same formula: the last map is the inclusion of the ordinary limit with zero shifted-product component. By [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], that inclusion for $J$ is the normalization of $H(D)\simeq R\lim D$. It follows that $u_N$ is precisely $[v_Q][q]^{-1}$ under the identification $H(D)\simeq\widehat N$. This is an equality of whole cone maps; equality of the projections alone is not used.

source.place: Clause (3): zero shifted-coordinate normalization of the unit, using Stacks Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok) and its normalized strict-cone refinement.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], inverse image along $g$ is reindexing by the site equivalence, and its constant-coefficient structure maps $c_n: g^{-1}B_{Y,n}\simeq B_{X,n}$ commute with all coefficient reductions. The completed structure map $c:g^{-1}\widehat R_Y\simeq\widehat R_X$ has $\pi_{X,n}c=c_n g^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})$. The completed-module functor $G$ transported along $c$ is exact by [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. It also preserves countable products: reindexing and the sectionwise computation of products [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] give $G(\prod M_n)(U)=\prod G(M_n)(U)$ on the underlying sheaves, and the module actions on both sides are transported by the same $c^{-1}$. Thus its canonical comparison $\phi_D:G(\prod D_n)\to\prod GD_n$, characterized by the projections, is an isomorphism. Additivity holds since reindexing preserves addition and zero sectionwise.

source.place: Clause (2): pullback under a scheme isomorphism and completed coefficient transport; the structure isomorphism and projection square in def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison.

proof.text: For each $n$ the termwise map $j_n:C_n\to GD_n$ is multiplication $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, with the scalar action transported through $c_n$. Its inverse is $i_n:x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Indeed $j_ni_n(x)=x$ and $i_nj_n(x\otimes a)=ax\otimes1=x\otimes a$ by balancing. These maps respect restrictions, so the formulas pass from the presheaf tensors to their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. They are $\widehat R_X$-linear because $\pi_{X,n}c=c_nG(\pi_{Y,n})$, and commute with differentials. On a transition, both composites send $x\otimes a$ to $\bar a\,G(\tau_n)x$, since the coefficient structure maps commute with reduction. Thus $j:C\xrightarrow{\sim}GD$ is an isomorphism of strict tower complexes, not only a list of derived isomorphisms. It is natural in chain maps $Q\to Q'$.

source.place: Clause (2): multiplication inverse to the tensor-unit map of def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison (a), compatibly with the transitions of (b).

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to $G$, using exactness and product preservation from step 4 and exact countable products from step 1. It supplies the specified natural comparison $\eta_D:GH(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(GD)$. By its normalization and [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], this map is $\phi_D$ on both cone coordinates, without an off-diagonal entry. In particular, $\phi_DG(1-s_D)=(1-s_{GD})\phi_D$, because projection to $n$ on either side is $G(\mathrm{pr}_n)-G(\tau_n)G(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})$. Since $j$ commutes strictly with transitions, $H(j):H(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(GD)$ is the product of the $j_n$ on both coordinates. Define $\theta_{g,N}=\eta_D^{-1}H(j):H(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}GH(D)$, read through the normalized identifications of step 1. This is the required direction $P_gN\to G\widehat N$.

source.place: Clauses (2)-(3): specified product/cone comparison on the entire strict quotient tower; Stacks Tag 0941 and the exact-product comparison refinement.

proof.text: By [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (b), the specified $\kappa^g_N$ is represented on $GQ$ by $w\mapsto(0,(i_nG(r_n)w)_n)$, followed by $[Gq]^{-1}$. Multiplication cancels each $i_n$, so $H(j)$ sends this chain map to $w\mapsto(0,(G(r_n)w)_n)$. The latter is exactly $\eta_DG(v_Q)$: its shifted coordinate is zero and its unshifted product has components $G(r_n)$. Applying $\eta_D^{-1}$ gives $G(v_Q)$ as an actual chain map. Step 3 and functoriality of exact $G$ therefore give $\theta_{g,N}\kappa^g_N=G([v_Q][q]^{-1})=G(u_N)$. This calculation fixes the shifted coordinate as well as the ordinary projections.

source.place: Clause (3): explicit comparison with the specified map in def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison (b), on both coordinates.

proof.text: For a chain map $f:Q\to Q'$ of flat-term K-flat complexes, the reductions satisfy $r'_nf=f_nr_n$, and multiplication gives $j'_ng^*(f_n)=G(f_n)j_n$. Consequently the square for $\theta$ commutes on each of the two product summands, by naturality of $\phi$; the square for the specified augmentation commutes by the first equality. The strict reduction construction is a derived functor by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The integral pullback descends from these representatives with its canonical resolution comparisons by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. The normalized limit comparison is natural on the derived tower category by [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Thus the chain-level squares descend to the localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: the equalities persist for inverses of inverted maps and for their composites. They give naturality for derived morphisms and identify $\theta$ under the canonical resolution comparisons for any two choices of $Q$. The specified $\kappa$ has the same independence and naturality, since $\kappa=\theta^{-1}G(u)$ and the actual adjunction unit $u$ is natural.

source.place: Clauses (2)-(3): resolution independence and naturality on entire derived systems; no uniqueness inferred from levelwise evaluations.

proof.text: Suppose $N$ is derived complete in the stated sense. Specialize [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] to $L=E$ and $Y$ unchanged. It asserts that the canonical completion map is an isomorphism for every such ambient complex; no boundedness or constructibility assumption occurs. After the multiplication identification $N\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}\widehat R_Y\simeq N$, its representative on $Q$ is $z\mapsto(0,(r_nz)_n)$, hence it is the actual $u_N$ by step 3. Therefore $G(u_N)$ and $\theta$ are isomorphisms, and $\kappa^g_N=\theta^{-1}G(u_N)$ is invertible with inverse $G(u_N)^{-1}\theta$. Both inverse identities follow by cancelling the adjacent inverse pairs. The completeness hypothesis is used only here; for an incomplete object the formula still holds but supplies no inverse to $u_N$.

source.place: Clause (3): Bhatt-Scholze Definition 3.5.2 and Proposition 3.5.1; L=E specialization of the existing scalar comparison identifies the actual canonical completion map.

proof_origin.place: Clauses (2)-(3), expanded to the specified strict quotient-cone comparison; supporting Stacks Tags 06YS, 08TC, 0941 and Bhatt-Scholze Definition 3.5.2 and Lemma 3.5.7(1).
